records.source: Καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς πάντας τοὺς λόγους τούτους, εἶπεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ·
records.gloss: And it happened when finished the Jesus all the words these, he said to the disciples of him:
pieces: When Jesus had finished all these words, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples,

L.1: And it happened, when Jesus had finished all these words, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples,

R.1: Jesus finished teaching all these things. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers,

decisions.choice: when Jesus had finished all these words: the formula that closes the last of the five long speeches
decisions.reason: Matthew ends each great speech this way (7:28; 11:1; 13:53; 19:1). Only here does he add "all", closing the speech of chapters 24-25 and perhaps the whole of Jesus's teaching before the passion.

decisions.choice: When Jesus had finished all these words
alternatives: When Jesus had finished saying all these things
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the wording of the same formula at 7:28.

records.heading: The plot against Jesus

records.source: Οἴδατε ὅτι μετὰ δύο ἡμέρας τὸ πάσχα γίνεται, καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδοται εἰς τὸ σταυρωθῆναι.
records.gloss: You know that after two days the Passover takes place, and the Son of the Man is handed over for the to be crucified.
pieces: "As you know, the Passover is two days away, and the Son of Man will be handed over to be crucified."

L.2: "You know that after two days the Passover comes, and the Son of Man is handed over to be crucified."

R.2: "You know that the Passover festival is two days from now. At that time the Son of Man will be handed over to be killed on a cross."

decisions.choice: the Passover: the yearly feast remembering Israel's rescue from Egypt
decisions.reason: The Passover lamb was killed on the fourteenth of the month Nisan and eaten that night (Exodus 12:1-14). The seven days of Unleavened Bread followed, and pilgrims crowded into Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: is handed over: given up to his enemies, by Judas and in God's plan
decisions.reason: The verb means to hand over. It is used of Judas (10:4; 26:15) and in Jesus's earlier predictions of his death (17:22; 20:18-19).

decisions.choice: is handed over: the present tense for what is certain to happen soon
alternatives: is being handed over at this moment
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of the coming event as already under way.

decisions.choice: will be handed over
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the future, since the event is two days away.

decisions.choice: to be killed on a cross; at that time
decisions.reason: Readable explains crucifixion and links the two events, as the "and" of the Greek implies.

records.source: Τότε συνήχθησαν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι τοῦ λαοῦ εἰς τὴν αὐλὴν τοῦ ἀρχιερέως τοῦ λεγομένου Καϊάφα, καὶ συνεβουλεύσαντο ἵνα τὸν Ἰησοῦν δόλῳ κρατήσωσιν καὶ ἀποκτείνωσιν·
records.gloss: Then were gathered the chief priests and the elders of the people in the courtyard of the high priest, the one called Caiaphas, \v 4 and they plotted together that the Jesus by deceit they might seize and kill;
pieces: Then the chief priests and the elders of the people met in the courtyard of the high priest, a man named Caiaphas.
There they made plans to arrest Jesus by some trick and put {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to death.

L.3: Then the chief priests and the elders of the people were gathered in the courtyard of the high priest, who was called Caiaphas,
L.4: and they plotted together to seize Jesus by deceit and kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.3: At that time the leading priests and the older leaders of the people met at the home of the high priest. His name was Caiaphas.
R.4: They made a plan to arrest Jesus secretly and kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: Caiaphas: high priest from about AD 18 to 36
decisions.reason: Joseph Caiaphas held the office longer than any other high priest under Roman rule. John 18:13 says he was the son-in-law of Annas, an earlier high priest.

decisions.choice: courtyard: the open court of the high priest's residence, or the residence itself
decisions.reason: The word means an enclosed courtyard and can stand for the whole palace around it. The same place appears in 26:58 and 26:69.

decisions.choice: by deceit: by stealth, away from the crowds
decisions.reason: They want to take him quietly, by some trick, for fear of the people (26:5).

decisions.choice: leading priests; older leaders
decisions.reason: Readable says who these groups were, as in 2:4.

records.source: ἔλεγον δέ· Μὴ ἐν τῇ ἑορτῇ, ἵνα μὴ θόρυβος γένηται ἐν τῷ λαῷ.
records.gloss: They were saying but, Not at the feast, so that not an uproar happens among the people.
pieces: But they kept saying, "Not at the festival. We do not want the people to riot."

L.5: But they were saying, "Not during the feast, so that there may not be an uproar among the people."

R.5: But they said, "We must not do it during the festival. The people might start a riot."

decisions.choice: an uproar among the people: the crowds of pilgrims, many of whom welcomed Jesus
decisions.reason: Jerusalem was crowded at Passover, and the crowds had hailed Jesus (21:8-11). The leaders had already held back for fear of them (21:46).

decisions.choice: not during the feast: not in the festival days
decisions.reason: The phrase may mean the days of the feast or the crowd gathered for it. Either way they want to avoid a public arrest; in the end Judas's offer lets them act at once.

decisions.choice: We do not want (B); The people might (R)
alternatives: so that there may not be
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the purpose clause into a plain statement of the leaders' fear.

records.source: Τοῦ δὲ Ἰησοῦ γενομένου ἐν Βηθανίᾳ ἐν οἰκίᾳ Σίμωνος τοῦ λεπροῦ, προσῆλθεν αὐτῷ γυνὴ ἔχουσα ἀλάβαστρον μύρου βαρυτίμου καὶ κατέχεεν ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτοῦ ἀνακειμένου.
records.gloss: The but Jesus being in Bethany in house of Simon the leper, \v 7 came to him a woman having an alabaster flask of ointment very costly and poured [it] on the head of him reclining.
pieces: While Jesus was at Bethany in the home of Simon, a man who had suffered from a skin disease,
a woman came up to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with an alabaster jar of very expensive perfumed oil. As {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sat at the table, she poured it over {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head.

L.6: Now while Jesus was in Bethany, in [the] house of Simon the leper,
L.7: a woman came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} having an alabaster jar of very costly ointment, and she poured [it] on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was reclining [at table].

R.6: Jesus was in the town of Bethany. He was at the house of a man named Simon, who had once had a bad skin disease.
R.7: While Jesus was eating there, a woman came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. She had a beautiful stone jar full of perfume that cost a great deal of money. She poured the perfume on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head.

decisions.choice: Simon the leper: known by a skin disease he had once had, probably healed
alternatives: a man still unclean with the disease
decisions.reason: A man still unclean could not have received guests at his table (Leviticus 13:45-46). The name may recall a past illness, perhaps one Jesus healed (8:2-3).

decisions.choice: an alabaster jar of very costly ointment: a sealed stone jar of perfumed oil
decisions.reason: Alabaster was a soft, translucent stone used for jars of perfume. Mark 14:3 says she broke the jar to pour it; Mark 14:5 values it at more than three hundred denarii, about a year's wages.

decisions.choice: poured it on his head: an act of honor, recalling the anointing of kings
decisions.reason: Oil was poured on a guest's head as an honor (Psalm 23:5), and kings were anointed on the head (1 Samuel 10:1). Jesus himself gives the act its meaning in 26:12.

decisions.choice: a man who had suffered from a skin disease (B); who had once had a bad skin disease (R)
decisions.reason: As in 8:2, Balanced and Readable describe the disease. Saying it was in the past follows meaning decision m1 and is not certain.

records.heading: A woman anoints Jesus at Bethany

records.source: ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ μαθηταὶ ἠγανάκτησαν λέγοντες· Εἰς τί ἡ ἀπώλεια αὕτη;
records.gloss: Having seen but the disciples were indignant saying, For what the waste this?
pieces: Seeing this, the disciples were indignant. They said, "What is the point of such waste?

L.8: But when the disciples saw [it], they were indignant, saying, "Why this waste?

R.8: When the followers saw this, they were upset. They said, "Why waste all that perfume?

decisions.choice: the disciples: Matthew speaks of the group
decisions.reason: John 12:4-6 names Judas as the one who complained. Matthew says the disciples as a whole objected.

decisions.choice: waste: loss, something thrown away
decisions.reason: The word means ruin or loss; here money poured out for nothing, as they see it.

records.source: ἐδύνατο γὰρ τοῦτο πραθῆναι πολλοῦ καὶ δοθῆναι πτωχοῖς.
records.gloss: Could for this to be sold for much and to be given to poor.
pieces: It could have been sold for a large sum and the money given to the poor."

L.9: For this could have been sold for much and given to [the] poor."

R.9: It could have been sold for a lot of money. Then the money could have been given to poor people."

decisions.choice: given to the poor: gifts to the poor were expected, especially at Passover
alternatives: a new idea of the disciples
decisions.reason: Giving to the poor was a duty of the law (Deuteronomy 15:11) and was linked with the feast (John 13:29).

decisions.choice: the money
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say that the money, not the perfume, would be given.

records.source: γνοὺς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τί κόπους παρέχετε τῇ γυναικί;
records.gloss: Having known but the Jesus said to them, Why troubles you cause to the woman?
pieces: Jesus was aware of this and said to them, "Why make trouble for this woman?

L.10: But Jesus, knowing [this], said to them, "Why do you cause the woman trouble?

R.10: Jesus knew what they were saying. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Why are you upsetting this woman?

decisions.choice: knowing this: Jesus became aware of their complaint
decisions.reason: Matthew does not say how he knew; they may have spoken openly.

decisions.choice: cause trouble: bother, distress
decisions.reason: The phrase means to give someone grief or annoyance, here by criticizing her.

records.source: ἔργον γὰρ καλὸν ἠργάσατο εἰς ἐμέ·
records.gloss: A work for good she worked for me;
pieces: What she has done for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is a beautiful thing.

L.10: For she has done a beautiful work for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

R.10: She has done a good and lovely thing for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: beautiful: good and fitting
alternatives: good only in the moral sense
decisions.reason: The word joins what is good with what is fine and fitting. Her act was right for the moment.

decisions.choice: good and lovely
decisions.reason: Readable gives both sides of the word.

records.source: πάντοτε γὰρ τοὺς πτωχοὺς ἔχετε μεθ’ ἑαυτῶν, ἐμὲ δὲ οὐ πάντοτε ἔχετε·
records.gloss: Always for the poor you have with yourselves, me but not always you have;
pieces: The poor will always be among you, but I will not always be with you.

L.11: For you always have the poor with you, but you do not always have {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

R.11: There will always be poor people among you. But I will not always be here with you.

decisions.choice: you always have the poor with you: Deuteronomy 15:11
decisions.reason: The law says the poor will never cease from the land, and so God's people must open their hand to them. Jesus does not set aside that duty.

decisions.choice: not always have me: Jesus points to his coming death
alternatives: he is leaving on a journey
decisions.reason: The time with him is short (26:2, 12), so honoring him now is fitting.

decisions.choice: I will not always be with you
alternatives: you do not always have me
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make Jesus the subject, which is more natural English.

records.source: βαλοῦσα γὰρ αὕτη τὸ μύρον τοῦτο ἐπὶ τοῦ σώματός μου πρὸς τὸ ἐνταφιάσαι με ἐποίησεν.
records.gloss: Having poured for this [woman] the ointment this on the body of me, for the to prepare for burial me she did [it].
pieces: By pouring this perfume over {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} body, she has made {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ready to be buried.

L.12: For in pouring this ointment on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} body, she did [it] to prepare {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for burial.

R.12: She put this perfume on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} body to get {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ready to be buried.

decisions.choice: to prepare me for burial: bodies were anointed with oil and spices for burial
decisions.reason: Jews anointed the dead before burial (Mark 16:1; John 19:39-40). Jesus says this anointing comes before his death.

decisions.choice: she did it for my burial: Jesus gives the act its meaning
alternatives: she knew he was about to die
decisions.reason: The words may mean that she intended it so, or that Jesus declares what her act means. The text does not say how much she understood.

records.source: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ὅπου ἐὰν κηρυχθῇ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦτο ἐν ὅλῳ τῷ κόσμῳ, λαληθήσεται καὶ ὃ ἐποίησεν αὕτη εἰς μνημόσυνον αὐτῆς.
records.gloss: Truly I say to you, wherever is proclaimed the gospel this in whole the world, will be spoken also what did this [woman] for a memorial of her.
pieces: Truly I tell you, in every place in the whole world where this gospel is proclaimed, people will also tell what she has done, so that she is remembered."

L.13: Truly I tell you, wherever this gospel is proclaimed in the whole world, what this [woman] has done will also be spoken of in memory of her."

R.13: I tell you the truth. This good news will be told all over the world. And wherever it is told, people will also tell what this woman did. They will remember her."

decisions.choice: this gospel: the good news of the kingdom, now including Jesus's death
decisions.reason: "Gospel" means good news (4:23; 24:14). "This" ties it to the death for which she has anointed him.

decisions.choice: the whole world: all nations and peoples
decisions.reason: As in 24:14 and 28:19, the good news is to go to every nation.

decisions.choice: in memory of her: so that she will be remembered
decisions.reason: The word can mean a reminder before God (Acts 10:4). Here the telling of her act keeps her memory alive among people.

decisions.choice: told
decisions.reason: Readable uses a simpler word for public announcing.

records.source: Τότε πορευθεὶς εἷς τῶν δώδεκα, ὁ λεγόμενος Ἰούδας Ἰσκαριώτης, πρὸς τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς εἶπεν· Τί θέλετέ μοι δοῦναι κἀγὼ ὑμῖν παραδώσω αὐτόν;
records.gloss: Then having gone one of the twelve, the one called Judas Iscariot, to the chief priests \v 15 said, What are you willing to me to give, and I to you will hand over him?
pieces: Then one of the Twelve, the man called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests
and asked, "How much will you pay me to hand {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to you?"

L.14: Then one of the Twelve, the [one] called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests
L.15: [and] said, "What are you willing to give me? And I will hand {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to you."

R.14: Then Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve followers, went to the leading priests.
R.15: He asked them, "What will you pay me if I hand {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to you?"

decisions.choice: then: Judas acts right after the anointing
decisions.reason: Matthew sets Judas's bargain beside the woman's costly gift and Jesus's talk of burial.

decisions.choice: hand him over: betray him to his enemies
alternatives: give him up in a lawful way
decisions.reason: The verb means to hand over. Used of Judas it means betrayal (10:4).

decisions.choice: what will you give me, and I will hand him over: a bargain
decisions.reason: The "and" links the price and the deed: give me something and I will do it.

decisions.choice: How much will you pay me (B); What will you pay me (R)
alternatives: What are you willing to give me
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the bargain plainly.

records.source: οἱ δὲ ἔστησαν αὐτῷ τριάκοντα ἀργύρια.
records.gloss: They and weighed out to him thirty silver pieces.
pieces: They paid him thirty silver coins.

L.15: And they weighed out to him thirty pieces of silver.

R.15: So they paid him thirty silver coins.

decisions.choice: weighed out: paid him the money
decisions.reason: The verb means to set or to weigh out, and it is the word for weighing wages in Zechariah 11:12. Mark 14:11 says they promised to give him money, and some take Matthew's word in that sense.

decisions.choice: thirty pieces of silver: Zechariah 11:12
decisions.reason: In Zechariah the shepherd's wages are thirty pieces of silver, a sum he calls a fine price, in scorn. Matthew returns to the passage in 27:9-10. Thirty shekels was also the price of a slave (Exodus 21:32).

decisions.choice: thirty pieces of silver: probably silver shekels, worth about four months' wages
decisions.reason: The coin is not named. If they were shekels, each worth about four denarii, the sum was about one hundred twenty days' wages for a laborer.

decisions.choice: thirty silver coins
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name coins. Because the coin is not named, no modern equivalent is given; meaning decision m3 gives the likely value. Literal keeps the familiar wording.

records.source: καὶ ἀπὸ τότε ἐζήτει εὐκαιρίαν ἵνα αὐτὸν παραδῷ.
records.gloss: And from then he was seeking opportunity that him he might hand over.
pieces: After that, Judas kept looking for the right moment to hand {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over.

L.16: And from then on he was seeking an opportunity to hand {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over.

R.16: From then on, Judas waited for a good time to hand Jesus over to them.

decisions.choice: opportunity: a fitting time, away from the crowds
decisions.reason: The leaders wanted to avoid an uproar (26:5). Judas looks for a time when Jesus is alone with his disciples.

decisions.choice: Judas (B, R); Jesus; to them (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Judas, and Readable also names Jesus, to make clear who is meant.

records.source: Τῇ δὲ πρώτῃ τῶν ἀζύμων προσῆλθον οἱ μαθηταὶ τῷ Ἰησοῦ λέγοντες· Ποῦ θέλεις ἑτοιμάσωμέν σοι φαγεῖν τὸ πάσχα;
records.gloss: On the and first of the unleavened [bread] came the disciples to the Jesus saying, Where do you want we prepare for you to eat the Passover?
pieces: On the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the disciples came to Jesus and asked, "Where would {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} like us to get the Passover meal ready for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?"

L.17: Now on the first [day] of Unleavened Bread the disciples came to Jesus, saying, "Where do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want us to prepare for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to eat the Passover?"

R.17: On the first day of the Festival of Bread Without Yeast, the followers came to Jesus. They asked, "Where do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want us to get the Passover meal ready for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?"

decisions.choice: the first day of Unleavened Bread: the day the Passover lambs were killed
alternatives: the day after the Passover meal
decisions.reason: Strictly the feast began on the fifteenth of Nisan, but the day the lambs were killed, the fourteenth, was counted with it (Mark 14:12). All yeast was removed from homes that day (Exodus 12:15-20).

decisions.choice: to eat the Passover: the meal of lamb, unleavened bread and bitter herbs
decisions.reason: The Passover was eaten at night in Jerusalem (Exodus 12:8; Deuteronomy 16:5-7). A room and food had to be made ready.

decisions.choice: Bread Without Yeast
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name of the feast.

decisions.choice: the Passover meal
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say that the meal is meant.

records.heading: The Passover with the Twelve

records.source: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ὑπάγετε εἰς τὴν πόλιν πρὸς τὸν δεῖνα καὶ εἴπατε αὐτῷ· Ὁ διδάσκαλος λέγει· Ὁ καιρός μου ἐγγύς ἐστιν· πρὸς σὲ ποιῶ τὸ πάσχα μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν μου.
records.gloss: He and said, Go into the city to such a one and say to him, The teacher says, The time of me near is; with you I do the Passover with the disciples of me.
pieces: He told them, "Go into the city to a certain man and tell him, 'The Teacher says: My appointed time is near. I will celebrate the Passover at your house with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} disciples.'"

L.18: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Go into the city to a certain man and say to him, 'The Teacher says: My time is near; at your [house] I am keeping the Passover with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} disciples.'"

R.18: Jesus answered, "Go into the city to a certain man. Say to him, 'The Teacher says: The time God has set for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is near. I will eat the Passover meal at your house with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} followers.'"

decisions.choice: a certain man: someone Matthew does not name
decisions.reason: The word is used of a person one does not name. He seems to know "the Teacher", so the meal may have been arranged beforehand.

decisions.choice: my time: the time God has appointed for Jesus's death
decisions.reason: The word means a fixed or fitting time. Jesus has just spoken of being handed over (26:2); compare "the hour" in 26:45.

decisions.choice: The time God has set for me
decisions.reason: Readable says whose appointment it is. That God set the time is implied by the word and the context.

records.source: καὶ ἐποίησαν οἱ μαθηταὶ ὡς συνέταξεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς, καὶ ἡτοίμασαν τὸ πάσχα.
records.gloss: And did the disciples as directed them the Jesus and prepared the Passover.
pieces: So the disciples followed Jesus's instructions and got the Passover meal ready.

L.19: And the disciples did as Jesus had directed them, and they prepared the Passover.

R.19: The followers did what Jesus told them. They prepared the Passover meal.

decisions.choice: prepared the Passover: arranged the room, the lamb and the food
decisions.reason: The lamb had to be killed at the temple in the afternoon, and the unleavened bread, wine and herbs made ready.

records.source: Ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης ἀνέκειτο μετὰ τῶν δώδεκα μαθητῶν καὶ ἐσθιόντων αὐτῶν εἶπεν· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι εἷς ἐξ ὑμῶν παραδώσει με.
records.gloss: Evening and having come he was reclining with the twelve disciples. \v 21 And eating of them he said, Truly I say to you that one of you will hand over me.
pieces: When evening came, Jesus took {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} place at the table with the twelve disciples.
During the meal {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Truly I tell you, one of you is going to betray {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

L.20: Now when evening came, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was reclining [at table] with the twelve disciples.
L.21: And while they were eating, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Truly I tell you that one of you will betray {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

R.20: In the evening Jesus was at the table with the twelve followers.
R.21: While they were eating, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "I tell you the truth. One of you is going to turn against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and hand {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} over to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} enemies."

decisions.choice: reclining: lying on couches around a low table, as at a feast
decisions.reason: At formal meals people reclined on their left side. At Passover even the poor reclined, as free people.

decisions.choice: betray: hand over to enemies
decisions.reason: The same verb as in 26:2 and 26:15. Coming from "one of you", the handing over is a betrayal.

decisions.choice: betray
decisions.reason: Where the verb is used of Judas's act, Literal and Balanced say "betray", as in 10:4.

decisions.choice: turn against me and hand me over to my enemies
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what betrayal means here.

records.source: καὶ λυπούμενοι σφόδρα ἤρξαντο λέγειν αὐτῷ εἷς ἕκαστος· Μήτι ἐγώ εἰμι, κύριε;
records.gloss: And being grieved exceedingly they began to say to him each one, Not I am [it], Lord?
pieces: They were deeply upset, and one after another they began to ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, it is not me, is it?"

L.22: And being exceedingly grieved, they began to say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, each one, "Surely it is not I, Lord?"

R.22: The followers were very sad. One by one they asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do not mean me, do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?"

decisions.choice: surely not I: a question that expects the answer no
decisions.reason: The form of the question hopes for "no". Each is anxious, yet none is sure of himself.

decisions.choice: Lord: the disciples' address of faith
decisions.reason: The eleven say "Lord"; Judas says "Rabbi" (26:25).

decisions.choice: it is not me, is it? (B); you do not mean me, do you? (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use an English question that also expects no.

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Ὁ ἐμβάψας μετ’ ἐμοῦ τὴν χεῖρα ἐν τῷ τρυβλίῳ οὗτός με παραδώσει·
records.gloss: He and answering said, The one having dipped with me the hand in the dish, this one me will hand over.
pieces: He replied, "Someone who has dipped his hand in the bowl along with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, he is the one who will betray {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.23: And answering, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "The [one] who has dipped the hand in the dish with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, he will betray {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

R.23: Jesus answered, "One of you who has eaten from the same bowl with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} will hand {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} over.

decisions.choice: the one who dipped with me: one who shares the meal, not a sign that points to one man
alternatives: a sign that names Judas to all
decisions.reason: Several shared each bowl. The words stress that the betrayer is a table companion, not that the others could tell who he was.

decisions.choice: betrayal by one who ate with him: Psalm 41:9
decisions.reason: The psalm speaks of a close friend who ate the singer's bread and turned against him. Eating together was a bond of trust.

decisions.choice: eaten from the same bowl
alternatives: dipped his hand in the dish
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what dipping in the dish means.

records.source: ὁ μὲν υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ὑπάγει καθὼς γέγραπται περὶ αὐτοῦ, οὐαὶ δὲ τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ ἐκείνῳ δι’ οὗ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδοται· καλὸν ἦν αὐτῷ εἰ οὐκ ἐγεννήθη ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος.
records.gloss: The indeed Son of the Man goes as it is written about him, woe but to the man that through whom the Son of the Man is handed over; good were it for him if not was born the man that.
pieces: The Son of Man goes on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} way as the Scriptures have written of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, but woe to the one through whom the Son of Man is betrayed! Better for that man if he had never been born."

L.24: The Son of Man goes as it is written about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, but woe to that man through whom the Son of Man is betrayed! It would be good for him if that man had not been born."

R.24: The Son of Man will die, just as the Scriptures say. But how terrible it will be for the man who hands over the Son of Man! It would be better for that man if he had never been born."

decisions.choice: goes as it is written: goes to his death, as the Scriptures say
decisions.reason: "Goes" is a way of speaking of death. Matthew does not name one passage here; compare 26:31, 54 and 56.

decisions.choice: God's plan and human guilt stand together
decisions.reason: That Scripture foretold the death does not lessen the guilt of the one who betrays him.

decisions.choice: better not born: his end will be worse than never having lived
decisions.reason: A strong saying of how terrible the judgment on the betrayer will be.

decisions.choice: will die, just as the Scriptures say
alternatives: goes as it is written about him
decisions.reason: Readable says what "goes" means here.

decisions.choice: how terrible it will be
decisions.reason: Readable explains the cry of woe; Literal and Balanced keep "woe", as in 11:21.

records.source: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ Ἰούδας ὁ παραδιδοὺς αὐτὸν εἶπεν· Μήτι ἐγώ εἰμι, ῥαββί;
records.gloss: Answering and Judas the one handing over him said, Not I am [it], rabbi?
pieces: Then Judas, who was betraying {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, said, "Rabbi, it is not me, is it?"

L.25: And Judas, the [one] betraying {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, answered, "Surely it is not I, Rabbi?"

R.25: Then Judas spoke. He was the one who was going to hand Jesus over. He said, "Teacher, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do not mean me, do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?"

decisions.choice: Rabbi: a title for a teacher, "my teacher"
decisions.reason: In Matthew only Judas calls Jesus "Rabbi" (here and 26:49), while the others say "Lord" (26:22). Jesus had told his disciples not to seek that title (23:7-8).

decisions.choice: Teacher
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the title.

records.source: λέγει αὐτῷ· Σὺ εἶπας.
records.gloss: He says to him, You said.
pieces: Jesus told him, "You have said it yourself."

L.25: He says to him, "You have said [so]."

R.25: Jesus said to him, "You have said it yourself."

decisions.choice: you have said so: yes, but in your words, not mine
decisions.reason: The phrase agrees with what was asked while putting the words back on the speaker. Here it tells Judas that Jesus knows. Jesus answers the high priest the same way in 26:64.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: yourself
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out the stress on "you" in the Greek.

records.source: Ἐσθιόντων δὲ αὐτῶν λαβὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἄρτον καὶ εὐλογήσας ἔκλασεν καὶ δοὺς τοῖς μαθηταῖς εἶπεν· Λάβετε φάγετε, τοῦτό ἐστιν τὸ σῶμά μου.
records.gloss: Eating and of them, having taken the Jesus bread and having blessed broke and having given to the disciples said, Take, eat, this is the body of me.
pieces: During the meal Jesus took a loaf, said the blessing, and broke it. He gave it to the disciples and said, "Take it and eat. This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} body."

L.26: And while they were eating, Jesus took bread, and after blessing [it] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} broke [it], and giving [it] to the disciples, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Take, eat; this is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} body."

R.26: While they were eating, Jesus took some bread. He thanked God for it and broke it into pieces. He gave it to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers and said, "Take this and eat it. This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} body."

decisions.choice: blessed: praised God over the bread, as at every Jewish meal
decisions.reason: The head of the meal said a blessing to God before breaking bread, as Jesus did when he fed the crowds (14:19). The cup is introduced with "giving thanks" (26:27).

decisions.choice: this is my body: the broken bread is his body given in death
alternatives: only a sign with no further meaning
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks at the Passover, where the food told of God's saving acts (Exodus 12:26-27). Christians have long differed over how the bread is his body; the words themselves say "is".

decisions.choice: thanked God for it
decisions.reason: Readable says to whom the blessing was spoken.

records.source: καὶ λαβὼν ποτήριον καὶ εὐχαριστήσας ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς λέγων· Πίετε ἐξ αὐτοῦ πάντες, τοῦτο γάρ ἐστιν τὸ αἷμά μου τῆς διαθήκης τὸ περὶ πολλῶν ἐκχυννόμενον εἰς ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν·
records.gloss: And having taken a cup and having given thanks he gave to them saying, Drink from it all, \v 28 this for is the blood of me of the covenant the for many being poured out for forgiveness of sins.
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took a cup, gave thanks, and passed it to them, saying, "Every one of you, drink from it.
For this is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant blood, poured out for many to bring forgiveness of sins.

L.27: And taking a cup and giving thanks, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave [it] to them, saying, "Drink from it, all [of you],
L.28: for this is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for [the] forgiveness of sins.

R.27: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took a cup of wine and thanked God for it. He gave it to them and said, "All of you drink from this cup.
R.28: This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} blood, which makes the covenant, God's agreement with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people. It is poured out for many people, so that their sins can be forgiven.

decisions.choice: my blood of the covenant: Exodus 24:8
decisions.reason: At Sinai Moses sprinkled the people with blood and said, "See the blood of the covenant." Jesus's death seals a covenant in the same way. Jeremiah 31:31-34 promised a new covenant with forgiveness of sins.

decisions.choice: the covenant, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the new covenant, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "the new covenant", probably from Luke 22:20 and 1 Corinthians 11:25. Several early manuscripts lack "new". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: poured out for many: Isaiah 53:12
decisions.reason: The servant "poured out his life to death" and "bore the sin of many". "Many" means a great number, as in 20:28.

decisions.choice: for the forgiveness of sins: his death brings forgiveness
decisions.reason: The angel said he would save his people from their sins (1:21). Here Jesus says how.

decisions.choice: a cup of wine; which makes the covenant, God's agreement with his people
decisions.reason: Readable says what was in the cup and what a covenant is.

records.source: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν, οὐ μὴ πίω ἀπ’ ἄρτι ἐκ τούτου τοῦ γενήματος τῆς ἀμπέλου ἕως τῆς ἡμέρας ἐκείνης ὅταν αὐτὸ πίνω μεθ’ ὑμῶν καινὸν ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ πατρός μου.
records.gloss: I say but to you, not not I will drink from now of this the fruit of the vine until the day that when it I drink with you new in the kingdom of the Father of me.
pieces: But I tell you this: from now on I will not drink this fruit of the vine again until the day comes when I share it with you, new, in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father's kingdom."

L.29: But I tell you, I will by no means drink of this fruit of the vine from now on until that day when I drink it new with you in the kingdom of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father."

R.29: I tell you, I will not drink wine again until the day when I drink it with you in a new way in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father's kingdom."

decisions.choice: the fruit of the vine: wine
decisions.reason: The phrase was used in the Jewish blessing spoken over wine.

decisions.choice: new: of a new kind, belonging to the age to come
decisions.reason: The word means new in quality. Jesus looks ahead to the feast of the kingdom (8:11; Isaiah 25:6).

decisions.choice: wine; in a new way
alternatives: this fruit of the vine; new
decisions.reason: Readable says what the phrase means and how "new" applies.

records.source: καὶ ὑμνήσαντες ἐξῆλθον εἰς τὸ Ὄρος τῶν Ἐλαιῶν.
records.gloss: And having sung a hymn they went out to the Mount of the Olives.
pieces: Then they sang a hymn and went out to the Mount of Olives.

L.30: And after singing a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.

R.30: They sang a song of praise. Then they went out to the Mount of Olives.

decisions.choice: a hymn: probably the psalms that closed the Passover meal
decisions.reason: Later Jewish practice sang Psalms 113-118 at Passover, ending with the last of them after the meal. Matthew does not say which song was sung.

decisions.choice: the Mount of Olives: the ridge east of Jerusalem
alternatives: a hill far from the city
decisions.reason: It lay across the Kidron Valley from the temple (21:1; 24:3).

decisions.choice: a song of praise
decisions.reason: Readable uses plainer words.

records.source: Τότε λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Πάντες ὑμεῖς σκανδαλισθήσεσθε ἐν ἐμοὶ ἐν τῇ νυκτὶ ταύτῃ, γέγραπται γάρ· Πατάξω τὸν ποιμένα, καὶ διασκορπισθήσονται τὰ πρόβατα τῆς ποίμνης·
records.gloss: Then says to them the Jesus, All you will be caused to stumble in me in the night this; it is written for, I will strike the shepherd, and will be scattered the sheep of the flock.
pieces: Then Jesus told them, "This very night every one of you will fall away because of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. For it is written: 'I will strike down the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will scatter in all directions.'

L.31: Then Jesus says to them, "All of you will fall away because of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} this night, for it is written, 'I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.'

R.31: Then Jesus said to them, "Tonight all of you will turn away and leave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. In the Scriptures God says, 'I will strike down the shepherd, and the sheep will run off in every direction.'

decisions.choice: fall away: stumble and desert him
decisions.reason: The verb pictures tripping over an obstacle (11:6; 13:21). That night they will abandon him (26:56).

decisions.choice: I will strike the shepherd: Zechariah 13:7
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew, God commands his sword to strike the shepherd. In Matthew's wording God himself says "I will strike". The "I" is God speaking.

decisions.choice: the shepherd and the sheep: Jesus and his disciples
decisions.reason: Jesus is the shepherd of God's people (2:6; 9:36). When he is struck, his followers scatter.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: In the Scriptures God says
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker of the quoted words, as meaning decision m2 explains.

records.source: μετὰ δὲ τὸ ἐγερθῆναί με προάξω ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν.
records.gloss: After but the being raised me I will go before you into the Galilee.
pieces: But after I have been raised, I will go to Galilee ahead of you."

L.32: But after I am raised, I will go ahead of you into Galilee."

R.32: But after God raises {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} from death, I will go to Galilee ahead of you."

decisions.choice: after I am raised: God will raise him
alternatives: after I rise by my own power
decisions.reason: The passive points to God as the one who acts (16:21; 17:23).

decisions.choice: go ahead of you: lead them, like a shepherd going before the flock
decisions.reason: After the scattering, the shepherd will gather them again. The promise is repeated in 28:7, 10 and kept in 28:16.

decisions.choice: God raises me from death
decisions.reason: Readable names the one who raises him.

records.source: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Πέτρος εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Εἰ πάντες σκανδαλισθήσονται ἐν σοί, ἐγὼ οὐδέποτε σκανδαλισθήσομαι.
records.gloss: Answering and the Peter said to him, If all will be caused to stumble in you, I never will be caused to stumble.
pieces: Peter answered, "The others may all fall away because of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, but I will never fall away."

L.33: But Peter answered and said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "If all fall away because of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, I will never fall away."

R.33: Peter said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "All the others may turn away from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. But I will never do that!"

decisions.choice: if all fall away, I never will: Peter sets himself above the others
decisions.reason: The "I" is stressed. Peter's boast prepares for his threefold denial (26:69-75).

records.source: ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἀμὴν λέγω σοι ὅτι ἐν ταύτῃ τῇ νυκτὶ πρὶν ἀλέκτορα φωνῆσαι τρὶς ἀπαρνήσῃ με.
records.gloss: Said to him the Jesus, Truly I say to you that in this the night before rooster to crow three times you will deny me.
pieces: Jesus told him, "Truly I tell you, three times this very night you will deny {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, before a rooster crows."

L.34: Jesus said to him, "Truly I tell you that this night, before a rooster crows, you will deny {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} three times."

R.34: Jesus said to him, "I tell you the truth. Tonight, before the rooster crows, you will say three times that you do not know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

decisions.choice: before a rooster crows: before dawn
decisions.reason: Roosters crow in the last hours of the night. Mark 13:35 names "cockcrow" among the watches of the night.

decisions.choice: deny me: disown me, say you do not know me
decisions.reason: As in 10:33. Peter's words in 26:70, 72 and 74 are exactly this.

decisions.choice: say that you do not know me
decisions.reason: Readable says what the denial will be.

records.source: λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Πέτρος· Κἂν δέῃ με σὺν σοὶ ἀποθανεῖν, οὐ μή σε ἀπαρνήσομαι.
records.gloss: Says to him the Peter, Even if it is necessary me with you to die, not not you I will deny.
pieces: But Peter insisted, "I will never deny {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, not even if it means dying with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}!"

L.35: Peter says to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Even if I must die with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, I will by no means deny {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

R.35: Peter said, "I will never say I do not know {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}! I will even die with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} if I have to!"

decisions.choice: by no means: the strongest form of denial
decisions.reason: Peter uses the double negative that Jesus used in 26:29.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: the promise first, the condition after
alternatives: Even if I must die with you
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put Peter's vow first for force.

records.source: ὁμοίως καὶ πάντες οἱ μαθηταὶ εἶπαν.
records.gloss: Likewise also all the disciples said.
pieces: Every one of the disciples said the same.

L.35: Likewise all the disciples also said [so].

R.35: All the other followers said the same thing.

decisions.choice: all the disciples: the same "all" who will flee
decisions.reason: Compare 26:56: "all the disciples left him and fled."

records.source: Τότε ἔρχεται μετ’ αὐτῶν ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς χωρίον λεγόμενον Γεθσημανὶ, καὶ λέγει τοῖς μαθηταῖς· Καθίσατε αὐτοῦ ἕως οὗ ἀπελθὼν ἐκεῖ προσεύξωμαι.
records.gloss: Then comes with them the Jesus to a place called Gethsemane, and he says to the disciples, Sit here until having gone away there I pray.
pieces: Jesus then came with them to a place named Gethsemane. He told the disciples, "Stay seated here while I go on over there and pray."

L.36: Then Jesus comes with them to a place called Gethsemane, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to the disciples, "Sit here while I go over there and pray."

R.36: Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers came to a place called Gethsemane. Jesus said to them, "Stay here. I am going over there to pray."

decisions.choice: Gethsemane: a plot of land on the Mount of Olives
decisions.reason: The name means "oil press". John 18:1 calls it a garden; it was likely an olive grove.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

records.heading: Jesus prays in Gethsemane

records.source: καὶ παραλαβὼν τὸν Πέτρον καὶ τοὺς δύο υἱοὺς Ζεβεδαίου ἤρξατο λυπεῖσθαι καὶ ἀδημονεῖν.
records.gloss: And having taken along the Peter and the two sons of Zebedee he began to be sorrowful and to be distressed.
pieces: He took Peter and Zebedee's two sons with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began to be filled with grief and anguish.

L.37: And taking along Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began to be sorrowful and deeply distressed.

R.37: He took Peter, James, and John with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Jesus began to feel very sad and troubled.

decisions.choice: Peter and the two sons of Zebedee: Peter, James and John
decisions.reason: The same three were with Jesus on the mountain where he was transfigured (17:1). The sons of Zebedee are James and John (4:21).

decisions.choice: deeply distressed: in anguish, overwhelmed
decisions.reason: The word describes deep inner turmoil.

decisions.choice: James, and John
decisions.reason: Readable names the two brothers.

records.source: τότε λέγει αὐτοῖς· Περίλυπός ἐστιν ἡ ψυχή μου ἕως θανάτου· μείνατε ὧδε καὶ γρηγορεῖτε μετ’ ἐμοῦ.
records.gloss: Then he says to them, Very sorrowful is the soul of me unto death; remain here and watch with me.
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "My soul is weighed down with grief, even to death. Stay here and keep awake with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

L.38: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to them, "My soul is very sorrowful, even to death; stay here and keep watch with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

R.38: He said to them, "My heart is so full of sadness that I feel I could die. Stay here and keep watch with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

decisions.choice: my soul is very sorrowful: Psalms 42-43
decisions.reason: The psalmist asks, "Why are you cast down, my soul?" (Psalm 42:5, 11; 43:5). Jesus uses the psalm's language for his grief.

decisions.choice: even to death: grief so heavy it could kill
alternatives: sorrow because death is near only
decisions.reason: The phrase measures the depth of the grief. Compare Jonah 4:9.

decisions.choice: keep watch: stay awake and alert
decisions.reason: The same verb is used in 24:42 and 25:13 for being ready.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: My heart is so full of sadness that I feel I could die
alternatives: My soul is very sorrowful, even to death
decisions.reason: Readable explains the saying.

records.source: καὶ προελθὼν μικρὸν ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ προσευχόμενος καὶ λέγων· Πάτερ μου, εἰ δυνατόν ἐστιν, παρελθάτω ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ τὸ ποτήριον τοῦτο· πλὴν οὐχ ὡς ἐγὼ θέλω ἀλλ’ ὡς σύ.
records.gloss: And having gone forward a little he fell on face of him praying and saying, Father of me, if possible it is, let pass from me the cup this; yet not as I will but as you.
pieces: He went a little farther, threw {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} face down on the ground, and prayed, "My Father, if there is any way, let this cup pass by {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. But not what I want; what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want."

L.39: And going a little farther, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} fell on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face, praying and saying, "My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; yet not as I will, but as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [will]."

R.39: He went a little farther and lay down with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face on the ground. He prayed, "My Father, if it is possible, do not make {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} drink this cup of suffering. But do what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want, not what I want."

decisions.choice: this cup: the suffering and death before him, as God's judgment on sin
decisions.reason: In the prophets the cup stands for God's anger poured out (Isaiah 51:17; Jeremiah 25:15). Jesus asked James and John whether they could drink his cup (20:22).

decisions.choice: fell on his face: lay face down in deep humility
decisions.reason: Lying face down was a posture of urgent prayer and submission.

decisions.choice: not as I will, but as you will: the verb is supplied from the first half
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves out the second "will". Jesus submits his will to his Father's.

decisions.choice: do not make me drink this cup of suffering
alternatives: let this cup pass from me
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the cup.

records.source: καὶ ἔρχεται πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς καὶ εὑρίσκει αὐτοὺς καθεύδοντας, καὶ λέγει τῷ Πέτρῳ· Οὕτως οὐκ ἰσχύσατε μίαν ὥραν γρηγορῆσαι μετ’ ἐμοῦ;
records.gloss: And he comes to the disciples and finds them sleeping, and says to the Peter, So not you were able one hour to watch with me?
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came back to the disciples and found them asleep. He said to Peter, "So none of you could stay awake with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for even one hour?

L.40: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes to the disciples and finds them sleeping, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to Peter, "So, you could not keep watch with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for one hour?

R.40: Then Jesus went back to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers and found them sleeping. He said to Peter, "Could you not stay awake with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for just one hour?

decisions.choice: you could not: plural, spoken to Peter for all three
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to Peter, who had boasted (26:33-35), but the verb is plural.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: none of you
decisions.reason: Balanced shows that the "you" is plural.

records.source: γρηγορεῖτε καὶ προσεύχεσθε, ἵνα μὴ εἰσέλθητε εἰς πειρασμόν· τὸ μὲν πνεῦμα πρόθυμον ἡ δὲ σὰρξ ἀσθενής.
records.gloss: Watch and pray, that not you enter into temptation; the indeed spirit willing, the but flesh weak.
pieces: Stay alert and pray that you will not come into testing. The spirit is eager, but human nature is weak."

L.41: Keep watch and pray, so that you may not enter into temptation; the spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak."

R.41: Stay awake and pray, so that you will not fail when you are tested. Your spirit wants to do what is right, but your human nature is weak."

decisions.choice: temptation: testing, a trial that could lead them to fall away
decisions.reason: As in the Lord's Prayer (6:13). The test that night is whether they will stand by Jesus.

decisions.choice: the spirit and the flesh: the willing human spirit and weak human nature
alternatives: God's Spirit and the human body
decisions.reason: The disciples truly mean their promises (26:35), but they are frail. Some take "spirit" as the Spirit God gives (Psalm 51:12).

decisions.choice: testing (B); fail when you are tested (R)
decisions.reason: As in 6:13, Balanced and Readable use the wider word; Literal keeps the traditional one.

decisions.choice: human nature
decisions.reason: "Flesh" here means human weakness, not the body alone.

records.source: πάλιν ἐκ δευτέρου ἀπελθὼν προσηύξατο λέγων· Πάτερ μου, εἰ οὐ δύναται τοῦτο παρελθεῖν ἐὰν μὴ αὐτὸ πίω, γενηθήτω τὸ θέλημά σου.
records.gloss: Again for a second time having gone away he prayed saying, Father of me, if not is possible this to pass if not it I drink, let be done the will of you.
pieces: He went away again, a second time, and prayed: "My Father, if there is no way for this to pass unless I drink it, then let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} will be done."

L.42: Again, for a second time, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went away and prayed, saying, "My Father, if this cannot pass unless I drink it, let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} will be done."

R.42: Jesus went away a second time and prayed, "My Father, if I must drink this cup of suffering, then let what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want be done."

decisions.choice: let your will be done: the words of the Lord's Prayer
decisions.reason: Jesus prays the words he taught his disciples (6:10).

decisions.choice: this, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: this cup, and from me, in many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "cup" and "from me", as in 26:39. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: if I must drink this cup of suffering
alternatives: if this cannot pass unless I drink it
decisions.reason: Readable states the condition positively and names the cup of 26:39.

records.source: καὶ ἐλθὼν πάλιν εὗρεν αὐτοὺς καθεύδοντας, ἦσαν γὰρ αὐτῶν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ βεβαρημένοι.
records.gloss: And having come again he found them sleeping, were for of them the eyes weighed down.
pieces: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came back, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} again found them asleep; they could not keep their eyes open.

L.43: And coming again, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} found them sleeping, for their eyes were heavy.

R.43: When Jesus came back, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} found them sleeping again. They were too tired to keep their eyes open.

decisions.choice: their eyes were heavy: they were overcome by sleep
decisions.reason: A common way of saying that sleep had overpowered them.

records.source: καὶ ἀφεὶς αὐτοὺς πάλιν ἀπελθὼν προσηύξατο ἐκ τρίτου τὸν αὐτὸν λόγον εἰπὼν πάλιν.
records.gloss: And having left them again having gone away he prayed a third time the same word having said again.
pieces: So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left them, went away once more, and prayed a third time, saying the same words.

L.44: And leaving them again, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went away and prayed a third time, saying the same word again.

R.44: So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left them and went away again. He prayed a third time, saying the same thing.

decisions.choice: the same word: the same prayer as before
decisions.reason: He prayed again as in 26:42.

records.source: τότε ἔρχεται πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Καθεύδετε τὸ λοιπὸν καὶ ἀναπαύεσθε· ἰδοὺ ἤγγικεν ἡ ὥρα καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδοται εἰς χεῖρας ἁμαρτωλῶν.
records.gloss: Then he comes to the disciples and says to them, Sleep the rest and take rest; behold, has drawn near the hour and the Son of the Man is handed over into hands of sinners.
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came to the disciples and said to them, "Go on sleeping, then, and resting. The hour is here: the Son of Man is being betrayed into the hands of sinners.

L.45: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes to the disciples and says to them, "Sleep on now and take your rest. Look, the hour has drawn near, and the Son of Man is betrayed into [the] hands of sinners.

R.45: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came back to the followers and said to them, "Sleep on, then, and rest! But now the time has come. The Son of Man is being handed over to sinners.

decisions.choice: sleep on and rest: a command, spoken with sorrow or irony
alternatives: a question: Are you still sleeping and resting?
decisions.reason: The words can be read as a command or as a question; the SBLGNT punctuation reads them as a statement. Either way Jesus tells them the time for watching is past, and in 26:46 he rouses them.

decisions.choice: the hour: the appointed time of his suffering
decisions.reason: Compare "my time" in 26:18.

decisions.choice: sinners: those who do not keep God's law, here the men coming to arrest him
decisions.reason: The word may also look ahead to the Gentiles to whom he will be handed over (20:19).

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

records.source: ἐγείρεσθε ἄγωμεν· ἰδοὺ ἤγγικεν ὁ παραδιδούς με.
records.gloss: Rise, let us go; behold, has drawn near the one handing over me.
pieces: Get up; let us be going. Here comes the man who is betraying {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

L.46: Get up, let us go. Look, the [one] who is betraying {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} has drawn near."

R.46: Get up! Let us go. The one who is handing {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} over is coming!"

decisions.choice: let us go: go to meet them
decisions.reason: Jesus does not flee; he goes out to face the one who betrays him.

decisions.choice: look (L); here comes (B); not rendered (R) (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

records.source: Καὶ ἔτι αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ἰδοὺ Ἰούδας εἷς τῶν δώδεκα ἦλθεν καὶ μετ’ αὐτοῦ ὄχλος πολὺς μετὰ μαχαιρῶν καὶ ξύλων ἀπὸ τῶν ἀρχιερέων καὶ πρεσβυτέρων τοῦ λαοῦ.
records.gloss: And still of him speaking, behold, Judas one of the twelve came, and with him a crowd great with swords and clubs from the chief priests and elders of the people.
pieces: Jesus had not finished speaking when Judas, one of the Twelve, came up. A large crowd came with him, carrying swords and clubs. The chief priests and the elders of the people had sent them.

L.47: And while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was still speaking, look, Judas, one of the Twelve, came, and with him a large crowd with swords and clubs, from the chief priests and elders of the people.

R.47: Jesus was still talking when Judas came. He was one of the twelve followers. A big crowd came with him. They carried swords and wooden clubs. The leading priests and older leaders of the people had sent them.

decisions.choice: a large crowd with swords and clubs: an armed band, probably the temple guard and servants of the chief priests
decisions.reason: They were sent by the chief priests, and the high priest's slave was among them (26:51). John 18:3 also mentions soldiers.

decisions.choice: one of the Twelve: Matthew stresses that the betrayer was one of his own
decisions.reason: Matthew has already told the reader who Judas is (10:4; 26:14). Repeating it here underlines the betrayal.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: the chief priests had sent them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "from" means.

records.heading: Judas's kiss and the arrest

records.source: ὁ δὲ παραδιδοὺς αὐτὸν ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς σημεῖον λέγων· Ὃν ἂν φιλήσω αὐτός ἐστιν· κρατήσατε αὐτόν.
records.gloss: The [one] and handing over him gave them a sign saying, Whom ever I kiss, he is; seize him.
pieces: The betrayer had given them a sign: "The man I kiss is the one you want. Arrest {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

L.48: Now the [one] betraying {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} had given them a sign, saying, "Whomever I kiss, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is [the one]; seize {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

R.48: Judas had given them a sign so they would know which man was Jesus. He had said, "The man I kiss is the one you want. Arrest {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

decisions.choice: kiss: the usual greeting of a disciple for his teacher
decisions.reason: A kiss was an ordinary sign of respect. In the dark and among many disciples, the armed band needed a way to know Jesus.

decisions.choice: had given: the sign was arranged beforehand
decisions.reason: The Greek past tense here describes something done earlier.

decisions.choice: so they would know which man was Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable says what the sign was for.

records.source: καὶ εὐθέως προσελθὼν τῷ Ἰησοῦ εἶπεν· Χαῖρε, ῥαββί· καὶ κατεφίλησεν αὐτόν.
records.gloss: And immediately having come to the Jesus he said, Greetings, rabbi, and kissed him.
pieces: Judas went straight to Jesus and said, "Greetings, Rabbi!" Then he kissed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.49: And immediately coming up to Jesus, he said, "Greetings, Rabbi!" and kissed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.49: Judas went right up to Jesus and said, "Hello, Teacher!" Then he kissed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: kissed him: perhaps kissed him warmly
decisions.reason: The verb is a stronger form of the one in 26:48. It may only mean that he carried out the sign.

decisions.choice: Rabbi: as in 26:25
decisions.reason: Judas again uses the title the others avoid.

decisions.choice: Hello, Teacher
decisions.reason: Readable uses an everyday greeting and gives the title's meaning, as in 26:25.

records.source: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἑταῖρε, ἐφ’ ὃ πάρει.
records.gloss: The and Jesus said to him, Friend, for what you are here.
pieces: Jesus said to him, "Friend, get on with what you are here for."

L.50: And Jesus said to him, "Friend, [do] that for which you have come."

R.50: Jesus said to him, "Friend, do what you came here to do."

decisions.choice: for what you are here: a command, "do what you came to do"
alternatives: a question: Friend, why are you here?
an exclamation: what you have come for!
decisions.reason: The Greek is short and unfinished. It is most likely a command, but the older reading as a question is possible.

decisions.choice: friend: companion, said with a note of reproach
decisions.reason: Matthew uses this word only when someone is in the wrong (20:13; 22:12).

records.source: τότε προσελθόντες ἐπέβαλον τὰς χεῖρας ἐπὶ τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ ἐκράτησαν αὐτόν.
records.gloss: Then having come they laid the hands on the Jesus and seized him.
pieces: At that, the crowd moved in. They laid hands on Jesus and arrested {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.50: Then they came and laid hands on Jesus and seized {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.50: Then the men came and grabbed Jesus. They arrested {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: laid hands on: took hold of by force
decisions.reason: Here the phrase means to seize someone.

records.source: καὶ ἰδοὺ εἷς τῶν μετὰ Ἰησοῦ ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα ἀπέσπασεν τὴν μάχαιραν αὐτοῦ καὶ πατάξας τὸν δοῦλον τοῦ ἀρχιερέως ἀφεῖλεν αὐτοῦ τὸ ὠτίον.
records.gloss: And behold, one of those with Jesus having stretched out the hand drew the sword of him and having struck the slave of the high priest cut off of him the ear.
pieces: One of the men with Jesus reached for his sword and drew it. He struck the high priest's servant and cut off his ear.

L.51: And look, one of those with Jesus stretched out [his] hand and drew his sword, and striking the slave of the high priest, he cut off his ear.

R.51: One of Jesus's followers pulled out his sword. He struck the high priest's servant and cut off the man's ear.

decisions.choice: one of those with Jesus: Matthew does not name him
decisions.reason: John 18:10 says it was Peter and names the slave Malchus.

decisions.choice: slave: a slave in the high priest's household
decisions.reason: He belonged to the high priest and was probably acting for him.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m2) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: τότε λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἀπόστρεψον τὴν μάχαιράν σου εἰς τὸν τόπον αὐτῆς, πάντες γὰρ οἱ λαβόντες μάχαιραν ἐν μαχαίρῃ ἀπολοῦνται·
records.gloss: Then says to him the Jesus, Return the sword of you into the place of it; all for those having taken sword by sword will perish.
pieces: Then Jesus told him, "Put your sword back where it belongs. Everyone who takes up the sword will die by the sword.

L.52: Then Jesus says to him, "Put your sword back into its place; for all who take [the] sword will perish by [the] sword.

R.52: Then Jesus said to him, "Put your sword away! People who use swords to fight will be killed with swords.

decisions.choice: all who take the sword will perish by the sword: violence brings violence in return
decisions.reason: A proverb. Compare Genesis 9:6.

decisions.choice: put your sword back: Jesus refuses to be defended by force
alternatives: he forbids all use of force
decisions.reason: He has taught his disciples not to repay evil with evil (5:39), and he goes to his death willingly (26:53-54).

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

records.source: ἢ δοκεῖς ὅτι οὐ δύναμαι παρακαλέσαι τὸν πατέρα μου, καὶ παραστήσει μοι ἄρτι πλείω δώδεκα λεγιῶνας ἀγγέλων;
records.gloss: Or do you think that not I am able to call upon the Father of me, and he will provide me now more than twelve legions of angels?
pieces: Do you not know that I could ask {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would send {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} more than twelve legions of angels right away?

L.53: Or do you think that I cannot call on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will at once provide {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} more than twelve legions of angels?

R.53: You know I could ask {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father for help. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would send {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} more than twelve armies of angels right away!

decisions.choice: legions: Roman army units of about six thousand men
decisions.reason: Twelve legions would be more than seventy thousand, a vast host of angels, more than one legion for each of the twelve disciples.

decisions.choice: Jesus could be rescued but chooses not to be
decisions.reason: He goes to his death of his own will, so that the Scriptures may be fulfilled (26:54).

decisions.choice: armies
decisions.reason: Readable explains the military word.

decisions.choice: Do you not know (B); You know (R)
alternatives: Or do you think that I cannot
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the negative question into a direct claim with the same force.

records.source: πῶς οὖν πληρωθῶσιν αἱ γραφαὶ ὅτι οὕτως δεῖ γενέσθαι;
records.gloss: How then would be fulfilled the Scriptures that thus it must happen?
pieces: But if I did, how could the Scriptures come true? They say that all this has to take place."

L.54: How then would the Scriptures be fulfilled, that it must happen this way?"

R.54: But if I did that, what the Scriptures say would not come true. They say these things must happen."

decisions.choice: it must happen: God's plan, written in the Scriptures
decisions.reason: "Must" speaks of God's will, as in 16:21.

decisions.choice: But if I did
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "then" refers back to.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
alternatives: How then would the Scriptures be fulfilled?
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer that they would not; Readable states it.

records.source: ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοῖς ὄχλοις· Ὡς ἐπὶ λῃστὴν ἐξήλθατε μετὰ μαχαιρῶν καὶ ξύλων συλλαβεῖν με;
records.gloss: In that the hour said the Jesus to the crowds, As against a robber you came out with swords and clubs to capture me?
pieces: Then Jesus said to the crowd, "Am I some bandit, that you come out with swords and clubs to seize {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?

L.55: At that hour Jesus said to the crowds, "Have you come out as against a robber, with swords and clubs, to capture {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?

R.55: Then Jesus said to the crowd, "Why do you come out with swords and clubs to arrest {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? Do you think I am a dangerous criminal?

decisions.choice: robber: a bandit, an armed outlaw
decisions.reason: The word is used of violent robbers and sometimes of rebels. Jesus is crucified between two such men (27:38).

decisions.choice: a dangerous criminal
decisions.reason: Readable gives the force of the word.

records.source: καθ’ ἡμέραν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἐκαθεζόμην διδάσκων καὶ οὐκ ἐκρατήσατέ με.
records.gloss: Every day in the temple I was sitting teaching and not you seized me.
pieces: Day after day I sat teaching in the temple courts, and you did not arrest {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} then."

L.55: Every day I sat in the temple teaching, and you did not seize {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

R.55: Every day I sat in the temple courtyard and taught the people. You did not arrest {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} then."

decisions.choice: I sat teaching: teachers sat to teach
decisions.reason: As in 5:1 and 13:2. He had taught openly in the temple courts (21:23).

decisions.choice: then
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out the contrast with now.

records.source: τοῦτο δὲ ὅλον γέγονεν ἵνα πληρωθῶσιν αἱ γραφαὶ τῶν προφητῶν.
records.gloss: This but all has happened that may be fulfilled the Scriptures of the prophets.
pieces: All this took place so that what the prophets wrote in the Scriptures would come true.

L.56: But all this has taken place so that the Scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled.

R.56: All of this happened to make the words of the prophets in the Scriptures come true.

decisions.choice: the narrator's comment, outside Jesus's speech
alternatives: the end of Jesus's words to the crowd
decisions.reason: The words can be read as Jesus's own (compare Mark 14:49). They are close to Matthew's own comments in 1:22 and 21:4, so the quotation closes before them.

decisions.choice: the Scriptures of the prophets: the prophetic writings as a whole
decisions.reason: Matthew does not name one passage; compare 26:31 and 26:54.

records.source: τότε οἱ μαθηταὶ πάντες ἀφέντες αὐτὸν ἔφυγον.
records.gloss: Then the disciples all having left him fled.
pieces: At that, every one of the disciples abandoned {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and ran off.

L.56: Then all the disciples left {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and fled.

R.56: Then all the followers left {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and ran away.

decisions.choice: the disciples fled: the scattering foretold in 26:31
decisions.reason: The sheep scatter when the shepherd is struck, as Jesus said.

records.source: Οἱ δὲ κρατήσαντες τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀπήγαγον πρὸς Καϊάφαν τὸν ἀρχιερέα, ὅπου οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι συνήχθησαν.
records.gloss: Those and having seized the Jesus led away to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and the elders were gathered.
pieces: The men who had arrested Jesus took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to Caiaphas the high priest. The scribes and the elders had gathered there.

L.57: And those who had seized Jesus led [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] away to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and the elders were gathered.

R.57: The men who arrested Jesus took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to the house of Caiaphas, the high priest. The teachers of the law and the older leaders were meeting there.

decisions.choice: where the scribes and the elders were gathered: the council met at night in the high priest's house
decisions.reason: The same place as in 26:3. A further meeting at dawn followed (27:1).

decisions.choice: the house of
decisions.reason: Readable says where they took him, as 26:58 shows.

records.heading: Jesus before the council

records.source: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἕως τῆς αὐλῆς τοῦ ἀρχιερέως, καὶ εἰσελθὼν ἔσω ἐκάθητο μετὰ τῶν ὑπηρετῶν ἰδεῖν τὸ τέλος.
records.gloss: The and Peter was following him from afar up to the courtyard of the high priest, and having entered inside he was sitting with the attendants to see the end.
pieces: Peter kept {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in sight from far behind and came as far as the high priest's courtyard. He went inside and took a seat among the guards, waiting to see what the end would be.

L.58: And Peter was following {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from a distance, as far as the courtyard of the high priest, and going inside, he sat with the guards to see the outcome.

R.58: Peter followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, staying far behind. He came to the courtyard of the high priest's house. He went in and sat with the guards. He wanted to see what would happen to Jesus.

decisions.choice: guards: attendants, the temple police and servants of the high priest
decisions.reason: The word is used of officers who serve a court or an official.

decisions.choice: the outcome: how the matter would end
decisions.reason: Peter wants to know what will be done to Jesus.

records.source: οἱ δὲ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ τὸ συνέδριον ὅλον ἐζήτουν ψευδομαρτυρίαν κατὰ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ὅπως αὐτὸν θανατώσωσιν, καὶ οὐχ εὗρον πολλῶν προσελθόντων ψευδομαρτύρων.
records.gloss: The and chief priests and the council whole were seeking false testimony against the Jesus so that him they might put to death, \v 60 and not they found, many having come forward false witnesses.
pieces: Meanwhile the chief priests and the whole council were trying to find false charges against Jesus that would get {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} executed.
Many false witnesses came forward, yet they found none.

L.59: Now the chief priests and the whole council were seeking false testimony against Jesus so that they might put {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to death,
L.60: and they did not find [any], though many false witnesses came forward.

R.59: The leading priests and the whole council wanted to kill Jesus. So they tried to find people who would tell lies about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
R.60: Many people came and told lies, but the council could not find anything to use against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: the council: the Sanhedrin, the highest Jewish court in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: It had about seventy members, chief priests, elders and scribes, with the high priest presiding.

decisions.choice: they did not find any: no testimony that would hold
alternatives: no one was willing to testify
decisions.reason: The law required two or three witnesses who agreed (Deuteronomy 19:15). Mark 14:56 says their testimony did not agree.

decisions.choice: anything to use against him
decisions.reason: Readable says what they failed to find.

records.source: ὕστερον δὲ προσελθόντες δύο εἶπαν· Οὗτος ἔφη· Δύναμαι καταλῦσαι τὸν ναὸν τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ διὰ τριῶν ἡμερῶν οἰκοδομῆσαι.
records.gloss: Later and having come two \v 61 said, This one said, I am able to destroy the temple of the God and through three days to build.
pieces: At last two of them stepped up
and stated, "This man claimed, 'I am able to tear down the temple of God and build it again within three days.'"

L.61: [and] said, "This [man] said, 'I am able to destroy the temple of God and to build [it] in three days.'"

R.60: At last two men came forward.
R.61: They said, "This man said, 'I can destroy God's temple and build it again in three days.'"

decisions.choice: two: the number of witnesses the law required
decisions.reason: Two agreeing witnesses were needed to convict (Deuteronomy 19:15).

decisions.choice: destroy the temple and build it in three days: a twisted form of Jesus's words
decisions.reason: Matthew records no such saying, though Jesus foretold the temple's destruction (24:2) and his rising on the third day. John 2:19 has Jesus say, "Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up."

decisions.choice: temple: the sanctuary itself
decisions.reason: The word means the holy house of God, not the courts around it.

records.source: καὶ ἀναστὰς ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Οὐδὲν ἀποκρίνῃ;
records.gloss: And having stood up the high priest said to him, Nothing you answer?
pieces: Then the high priest stood up and said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} no answer?

L.62: And the high priest stood up and said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} answer nothing?

R.62: Then the high priest stood up and said to Jesus, "Do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have nothing to say?

decisions.choice: two questions: "Do you answer nothing? What is it these testify?"
alternatives: one question: Do you answer nothing to what these testify against you?
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads two questions. The meaning is nearly the same either way.

records.source: τί οὗτοί σου καταμαρτυροῦσιν;
records.gloss: What these you testify against?
pieces: What about the evidence these men are bringing against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?"

L.62: What is it that these testify against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?"

R.62: What do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} say about these things they are saying against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?"

decisions.choice: What about the evidence (B); What do you say about (R)
alternatives: What is it that these testify
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that the high priest is pressing Jesus to reply.

records.source: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἐσιώπα.
records.gloss: The and Jesus was silent.
pieces: Jesus, however, said nothing.

R.63: But Jesus did not say anything.

decisions.choice: kept silent: like the servant of Isaiah 53:7
decisions.reason: The servant "did not open his mouth" before those who afflicted him. Matthew does not cite the verse here.

records.source: καὶ ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἐξορκίζω σε κατὰ τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ζῶντος ἵνα ἡμῖν εἴπῃς εἰ σὺ εἶ ὁ χριστὸς ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ.
records.gloss: And the high priest said to him, I adjure you by the God the living that to us you say if you are the Christ the Son of the God.
pieces: Then the high priest said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "In the name of the living God I place {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} under oath. Tell us: are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, the Son of God?"

L.63: And the high priest said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "I put {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} under oath by the living God that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} tell us whether {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, the Son of God."

R.63: The high priest said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Swear by the living God and tell us: Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, the Son of God?"

decisions.choice: I put you under oath: a formal demand that he answer before God
decisions.reason: Someone put under oath was bound to speak (Leviticus 5:1). Jesus, who had kept silent, now answers.

decisions.choice: the Christ, the Son of God: the Messiah, God's chosen king
decisions.reason: God called Israel's king his son (Psalm 2:7; 2 Samuel 7:14). The high priest uses the words of the confession Peter made (16:16).

decisions.choice: Swear by the living God and tell us
alternatives: I put you under oath by the living God
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what being put under oath means.

records.source: λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Σὺ εἶπας· πλὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀπ’ ἄρτι ὄψεσθε τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου καθήμενον ἐκ δεξιῶν τῆς δυνάμεως καὶ ἐρχόμενον ἐπὶ τῶν νεφελῶν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ.
records.gloss: Says to him the Jesus, You said; yet I say to you, from now you will see the Son of the Man sitting at right of the Power and coming on the clouds of the heaven.
pieces: Jesus answered him, "You have said it yourself. Yet this I tell you all: from this time on, you will see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of the Power, and coming on the clouds of heaven."

L.64: Jesus says to him, "You have said [so]. But I tell you, from now on you will see the Son of Man sitting at [the] right hand of the Power and coming on the clouds of heaven."

R.64: Jesus said to him, "You have said it yourself. But I tell all of you: After this you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right side of God, the Power. And you will see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} coming on the clouds of heaven."

decisions.choice: you have said so: yes, but in your words
decisions.reason: As in 26:25. Jesus accepts the title but goes on to say in his own words who he is.

decisions.choice: seated at the right hand, coming on the clouds: Psalm 110:1 and Daniel 7:13
decisions.reason: In Psalm 110:1 the Lord tells David's lord to sit at his right hand. In Daniel 7:13 one like a son of man comes with the clouds of heaven to receive a kingdom. Jesus joins the two (compare 22:44 and 24:30).

decisions.choice: the Power: a reverent way of saying God
decisions.reason: Jews often avoided saying God's name and spoke of him by titles such as this.

decisions.choice: from now on: from this point his exaltation begins
alternatives: only at the end of the age
decisions.reason: The "you" is plural. His judges will see him exalted, beginning with his death and resurrection and completed when he comes.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: God, the Power
decisions.reason: Readable says who "the Power" is.

records.source: τότε ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς διέρρηξεν τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ λέγων· Ἐβλασφήμησεν· τί ἔτι χρείαν ἔχομεν μαρτύρων;
