records.gloss: Then the high priest tore the garments of him saying, He blasphemed; why still need have we of witnesses?
pieces: The high priest then ripped his robes and cried, "This is blasphemy! What use do we have for more witnesses?

L.65: Then the high priest tore his garments, saying, "He has blasphemed! What further need do we have of witnesses?

R.65: Then the high priest tore his clothes to show how upset he was. He said, "He has insulted God! We do not need any more witnesses!

decisions.choice: tore his garments: a sign of grief and horror
decisions.reason: People tore their clothes on hearing words against God (2 Kings 18:37-19:1).

decisions.choice: blasphemed: insulted God by claiming what belongs to God
decisions.reason: As in 9:3. To claim a seat at God's right hand was, to the high priest, a claim to share God's honor (Leviticus 24:16).

decisions.choice: to show how upset he was
decisions.reason: Readable explains the gesture.

records.source: ἴδε νῦν ἠκούσατε τὴν βλασφημίαν·
records.gloss: Behold now you heard the blasphemy.
pieces: You have now heard the blasphemy yourselves.

L.65: Look, now you have heard the blasphemy.

R.65: You all just heard {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} insult God.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: heard him insult God
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word, as in 26:65.

records.source: τί ὑμῖν δοκεῖ;
records.gloss: What to you seems?
pieces: What is your verdict?"

decisions.choice: what do you think: a call for a verdict
decisions.reason: The high priest asks the council to decide (compare Mark 14:64).

records.source: οἱ δὲ ἀποκριθέντες εἶπαν· Ἔνοχος θανάτου ἐστίν.
records.gloss: They and answering said, Liable of death he is.
pieces: They answered, "He deserves to die."

L.66: And they answered and said, "He is deserving of death."

R.66: They answered, "He should be put to death!"

decisions.choice: deserving of death: guilty of a crime that carries the death penalty
decisions.reason: The law punished blasphemy with death (Leviticus 24:16). Under Roman rule the council could not carry out a death sentence itself, so they hand Jesus to Pilate (27:1-2; John 18:31).

records.source: τότε ἐνέπτυσαν εἰς τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐκολάφισαν αὐτόν, οἱ δὲ ἐράπισαν λέγοντες· Προφήτευσον ἡμῖν, χριστέ, τίς ἐστιν ὁ παίσας σε;
records.gloss: Then they spat into the face of him and struck him, others and slapped \v 68 saying, Prophesy to us, Christ, who is the one having struck you?
pieces: Next they spat in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face and pounded {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with their fists, while others struck {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with open hands
and jeered, "Prophesy for us, {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}! Which one of us hit {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?"

L.67: Then they spat in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face and struck {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and others slapped [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}],
L.68: saying, "Prophesy to us, {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}! Who is it that struck {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?"

R.67: Then some of them spat in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face and hit {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with their fists. Others slapped {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
R.68: They said, "Show us {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are a prophet, {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}! Tell us who hit {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}!"

decisions.choice: they: members of the council, and perhaps the guards with them
decisions.reason: Matthew does not say who; Mark 14:65 adds the guards.

decisions.choice: prophesy, who struck you: a mocking test of a prophet
decisions.reason: Mark 14:65 and Luke 22:64 say they covered his face. Matthew does not mention it, but the taunt assumes he could not see who hit him.

decisions.choice: spitting and striking: Isaiah 50:6
decisions.reason: The servant says, "I did not hide my face from shame and spitting." Jesus had foretold this mocking (20:19).

decisions.choice: Show us you are a prophet
decisions.reason: Readable says what the taunt demands.

records.source: Ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἐκάθητο ἔξω ἐν τῇ αὐλῇ· καὶ προσῆλθεν αὐτῷ μία παιδίσκη λέγουσα· Καὶ σὺ ἦσθα μετὰ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Γαλιλαίου·
records.gloss: The and Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard; and came to him one servant girl saying, Also you were with Jesus the Galilean.
pieces: Meanwhile Peter was sitting out in the courtyard. A servant girl came up to him and said, "You were with Jesus the Galilean too."

L.69: Now Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard, and a servant girl came to him, saying, "You too were with Jesus the Galilean."

R.69: Peter was still sitting outside in the courtyard. A young woman who worked there came to him. She said, "You were with Jesus, the man from Galilee!"

decisions.choice: servant girl: a young female slave or servant of the household
decisions.reason: She belonged to the high priest's household.

decisions.choice: outside: in the open courtyard, outside the room where Jesus was being tried
decisions.reason: Peter had come inside the gate (26:58); the trial went on in the house.

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἠρνήσατο ἔμπροσθεν πάντων λέγων· Οὐκ οἶδα τί λέγεις.
records.gloss: He and denied before all saying, Not I know what you say.
pieces: But Peter denied it with everyone listening. "I have no idea what you mean," he said.

L.70: But he denied [it] before them all, saying, "I do not know what you are saying."

R.70: But Peter said in front of everyone, "I do not know what you are talking about!"

decisions.choice: I do not know what you are saying: a way of brushing off the charge
decisions.reason: Peter pretends not to understand rather than answer.

decisions.choice: before them all: a public denial
decisions.reason: Compare 10:33: whoever denies Jesus before people.

records.source: ἐξελθόντα δὲ εἰς τὸν πυλῶνα εἶδεν αὐτὸν ἄλλη καὶ λέγει τοῖς ἐκεῖ· Οὗτος ἦν μετὰ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Ναζωραίου·
records.gloss: Having gone out and to the gateway saw him another and says to those there, This one was with Jesus the Nazarene.
pieces: He went out toward the gateway, where another servant girl saw him and told the people there, "This man was with Jesus of Nazareth."

L.71: And when he had gone out to the gateway, another [servant girl] saw him and says to those there, "This [man] was with Jesus the Nazarene."

R.71: Then Peter went out to the gate. Another servant girl saw him there. She said to the people standing there, "This man was with Jesus from Nazareth."

decisions.choice: the Nazarene: the man from Nazareth
decisions.reason: Jesus grew up in Nazareth (2:23).

decisions.choice: the gateway: the entrance passage from the street into the courtyard
decisions.reason: Peter moves away from the fire toward the way out.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

records.source: καὶ πάλιν ἠρνήσατο μετὰ ὅρκου ὅτι Οὐκ οἶδα τὸν ἄνθρωπον.
records.gloss: And again he denied with an oath, Not I know the man.
pieces: Again he denied it, this time with an oath: "I do not know the man!"

L.72: And again he denied [it] with an oath, "I do not know the man."

R.72: Again Peter said it was not true. He made a promise before God and said, "I do not know that man!"

decisions.choice: with an oath: calling on God as witness
decisions.reason: An oath called on God to confirm one's words. Jesus had taught his disciples not to swear at all (5:34-37).

decisions.choice: the man: Peter will not even say Jesus's name
decisions.reason: He speaks of Jesus as a stranger.

decisions.choice: made a promise before God
decisions.reason: Readable explains what an oath is.

records.source: μετὰ μικρὸν δὲ προσελθόντες οἱ ἑστῶτες εἶπον τῷ Πέτρῳ· Ἀληθῶς καὶ σὺ ἐξ αὐτῶν εἶ, καὶ γὰρ ἡ λαλιά σου δῆλόν σε ποιεῖ·
records.gloss: After a little and having come those standing said to the Peter, Truly also you of them are, also for the speech of you evident you makes.
pieces: Before long the people standing nearby came up to Peter. "You are certainly one of them," they said. "The way you talk betrays you."

L.73: And after a little [while], those standing [there] came and said to Peter, "Truly you too are [one] of them, for even your speech makes you evident."

R.73: A little later, the people standing there came to Peter. They said, "We are sure you are one of Jesus's followers. We can tell from the way you talk that you are from Galilee."

decisions.choice: your speech: Peter's Galilean way of speaking
decisions.reason: Galileans spoke with an accent that people in Jerusalem could recognize. Jesus and his disciples were known to come from Galilee (26:69).

decisions.choice: one of Jesus's followers; that you are from Galilee
alternatives: one of them; your speech makes you evident
decisions.reason: Readable says who "them" are and what his speech showed.

records.source: τότε ἤρξατο καταθεματίζειν καὶ ὀμνύειν ὅτι Οὐκ οἶδα τὸν ἄνθρωπον.
records.gloss: Then he began to curse and to swear, Not I know the man.
pieces: Then he began cursing and swearing, "I do not know the man!"

L.74: Then he began to call down curses and to swear, "I do not know the man!"

R.74: Then Peter began to curse. He swore an oath and said, "I do not know the man!"

decisions.choice: to call down curses: probably on himself if he was lying
decisions.reason: The verb means to invoke a curse, but Matthew does not say on whom. It may be on himself, as an oath of denial, or on Jesus.

decisions.choice: the third denial is the strongest
alternatives: the same as the first two
decisions.reason: A plain denial (26:70), then an oath (26:72), now curses and an oath.

records.source: καὶ εὐθέως ἀλέκτωρ ἐφώνησεν·
records.gloss: And immediately a rooster crowed.
pieces: At that very moment a rooster crowed.

decisions.choice: immediately: the sign Jesus foretold comes at once
decisions.reason: The crowing comes just as Peter finishes his third denial (26:34).

records.source: καὶ ἐμνήσθη ὁ Πέτρος τοῦ ῥήματος Ἰησοῦ εἰρηκότος ὅτι Πρὶν ἀλέκτορα φωνῆσαι τρὶς ἀπαρνήσῃ με, καὶ ἐξελθὼν ἔξω ἔκλαυσεν πικρῶς.
records.gloss: And remembered the Peter the word of Jesus having said, Before rooster to crow three times you will deny me; and having gone outside he wept bitterly.
pieces: Then Peter remembered what Jesus had told him: "Before a rooster crows, you will deny {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} three times." And he went outside and broke down in bitter tears.

L.75: And Peter remembered the word of Jesus, who had said, "Before a rooster crows, you will deny {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} three times." And he went outside and wept bitterly.

R.75: Peter remembered what Jesus had said: "Before the rooster crows, you will say three times that you do not know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}." Peter went outside and cried very hard.

decisions.choice: the word of Jesus: his warning in 26:34, now fulfilled
decisions.reason: Matthew repeats the words of 26:34 so the reader sees them come true.

decisions.choice: wept bitterly: deep grief over what he had done
decisions.reason: Peter's sorrow stands in contrast with Judas's end (27:3-5).

decisions.choice: broke down in bitter tears
decisions.reason: Balanced uses current English with the same force.
